steps.text:
I expect 4Q standalone sales of ¥7,360m and operating income of ¥2,260m. Sales should be fairly accurate, but the gross margin is uncertain, so overall confidence is medium.

**Sales.** Monthly sales from April to June 2026 add up to ¥7,325m: April ¥2,453m, May ¥2,531m and June ¥2,342m. That is up 25.8% on the same three months last year. Over the past quarters, reported sales have run 0.2–1.1% above the monthly totals:

| Quarter | Reported ÷ monthly total |
|---|---|
| FY25 4Q | 5,851.3 ÷ 5,822.3 = 1.005 |
| FY26 2Q | 7,164.0 ÷ 7,152.3 = 1.002 |
| FY26 3Q | 5,314.9 ÷ 5,258.3 = 1.011 |

Using about 1.005 gives ¥7,360m. May was very strong because customers came in early ahead of the 8% service price rise on June 1, 2026 (Q3 briefing p.10). Sales of products to dealers and repair shops also stayed strong through May and June.

**Gross profit.** 4Q gross margin was 52.0% last year (FY25) and 54.3% the year before (FY24). This year the underlying margin has been running about 3–4 points lower: 1Q 46.9% (prior year 49.9%) and 2Q 54.4% (58.5%). 3Q fell to 35.0%, but that included a special bonus that seems to have landed largely in cost of sales. Two things should help in 4Q: sales up 26% spread over fairly fixed store labour costs, and a higher share of products, which have higher margins. I assume 51.1%, so gross profit ≈ ¥3,760m.

**SG&A.** Last year's 4Q SG&A of ¥1,311.8m, grown about 10% (the 1Q rate), gives about ¥1,443m. I add about ¥60m for growth investments funded by the ¥6,762m securities gain booked in 2Q. Spending on these was ¥453m in 2Q and ¥640m in 3Q, and the April–June TV programme costs ¥90m. Total SG&A ≈ ¥1,500m.

**Operating income.** ¥3,760m − ¥1,500m = ¥2,260m, about 31% above last year's 4Q (¥1,728.5m). The company's full-year guidance, which it kept unchanged at 3Q, implies a 4Q of ¥8,047m sales and ¥3,008m operating income. Monthly sales already show 4Q will fall well short of that, so I expect operating income to miss guidance as well.
